children: Export orders across key cable manufacturers are expected to provide revenue visibility in the second half of FY27, with KEI Industries holding Rs 991 crore of export orders and Polycab reporting a strong pipeline across major international markets

India’s wires and cables industry is expected to draw support from a strong export order pipeline in the second half of FY27, even as domestic demand and volume growth remain uneven across companies, according to a report by Kotak Institutional Equities.

Exports remain a bright spot for the sector, with several manufacturers carrying substantial orders scheduled for execution in the coming months. KEI Industries had export orders worth Rs 991 crore, which are expected to be executed within three to four months, while its overall order book grew 36 per cent year-on-year to Rs 5,200 crore.

The export opportunity is also reflected in Polycab’s order pipeline. The company reported strong orders across the US, Europe, Latin America and Asia, with demand spanning low-voltage, medium-voltage and high-voltage cables. The orders are being driven by requirements from data centres, artificial intelligence infrastructure and the energy transition, Kotak said.

Polycab’s exports accounted for around 32 per cent of its overall sales and grew 80 per cent year-on-year in the September quarter. The export mix also shifted towards cables. However, the company reported mid-to-high single-digit overall volume growth in its wires and cables business, against a high base in the year-ago quarter.

Havells also reported export growth, with exports increasing 7.1 per cent year-on-year to Rs 460 crore. The US accounted for around half of its export order book, while the remaining orders came from the Middle East and Australia. Its wires and cables business grew 40 per cent during the quarter, supported by broad-based demand.

KEI Industries reported an overall order book of Rs 5,200 crore at the end of the quarter, up 36 per cent year-on-year. Its wires and cables business accounted for Rs 4,930 crore of the total, while export orders stood at Rs 991 crore. These export orders are expected to be executed over the next three to four months.

Apar Industries also reported a near-doubling of its cables order book to Rs 3,000 crore, compared with Rs 1,650 crore earlier. The order book includes around Rs 1,000 crore from Google's US data centre, including a single order worth more than Rs 500 crore, as well as orders linked to Amazon's largest data centre in India. The bulk of these orders, including data-centre-related orders, is expected to be executed by March 2027.

The broader sector, however, continues to face differences in volume performance across companies. Kotak noted that wires and cables companies registered 46 per cent year-on-year value growth in the second quarter, largely driven by inflationary commodity prices, while volume growth remained weak for most players, with Diamond Power Infrastructure being an exception.

Diamond Power reported underlying volume growth of 60-70 per cent during the quarter, supported by demand for medium-voltage and extra-high-voltage cables, as well as conductors. Its order book stood at Rs 3,700 crore, although the company expects a more significant contribution from exports from FY28.

Kotak's assessment points to export orders providing an important source of revenue visibility for the industry in the second half of FY27, even as companies navigate uneven volume growth, execution timelines, and changing demand conditions.
